chunks: And in the Nawadir of Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them, that he said:
Regarding a man performing tawaf when a need arises for him:

He said: “There is no harm in his going to attend to his own need or the need of someone else and interrupting the tawaf. And if he wishes to rest during his tawaf and sit, there is no harm in that. Then when he returns, he continues his tawaf from where he left off, even if it was less than half.”

key_terms.بَنَى عَلَى طَوَافِهِ: he continues his tawaf from the point already reached
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; an expression indicating permissibility
key_terms.يَسْتَرِيحَ: to rest during the performance of tawaf
key_terms.يَقْطَعَ: to interrupt or break off the action temporarily
key_terms.ٱلطَّوَافَ: tawaf, the ritual circumambulation around the Ka'bah
key_terms.ٱلنِّصْفِ: half; here referring to half of the tawaf rounds
key_terms.ٱلْحَاجَةُ: a need or necessary matter that arises during the ritual

ai.seo_question: Can a person interrupt tawaf for a need or rest and then continue from where he stopped?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one performing tawaf whose circumambulation is interrupted by a personal need, another person's need, or by resting. It states that such an interruption does not invalidate the tawaf, and the person may resume and continue from where he stopped, even if he had completed less than half.
